dwelling_rules.action_text: Keep your phone charged, keep drinking water and documents ready, and follow official instructions.
Move documents, medicines and food to a high shelf. Switch off the main power if water enters. Do not walk or drive through moving water.
Leave now for higher ground or a shelter. Your lane floods first. Take documents, medicines, a torch and drinking water.
Move valuables and food to an upper floor or a neighbour's roof access now. Switch off the main power before water reaches the sockets.
You have more time than ground-floor neighbours, but keep the same items ready. Check on them and help if you can.
Stay on your floor. Do not use the lift or basement parking. Store two days of drinking water; supply may stop.
A mud or tin-roofed home floods fastest and can weaken. Move to a concrete building or official shelter now, don't wait for water to enter.
You are likely safe where you are. Stay in, keep roads clear for rescue, and check on neighbours in low-lying lanes.
Stay indoors away from windows. Tie down loose objects on the roof and balcony. Keep a torch and radio ready; power will likely go.
Move to a cyclone shelter before landfall. Storm surge and rain will flood your lane fastest.
Move to an inner room or corridor away from glass. Upper floors feel stronger winds. Do not use the lift once power is unstable.
A kutcha roof will not hold in strong wind. Move to the nearest concrete building or cyclone shelter well before landfall.
Stay indoors away from windows and secure loose roofing or sheets, storm surge is less of a risk for you but wind still is.
Avoid underpasses and open drains. Keep outdoor trips short and carry your phone charged.
Water can rise quickly in your lane. Move essentials up now and be ready to leave if water crosses the doorstep.
Block door gaps, lift electrical items off the floor, and keep the main switch within reach.
Check your roof and walls for leaks or softening. Move to a stronger neighbour's home if water is getting in.
Stay indoors from noon to 4pm. Drink water every hour even if not thirsty. Dizziness, confusion or no sweating needs a doctor.
Top floors heat up the most. Move to a lower floor or shaded room in the afternoon and keep curtains closed.
A tin or thatched roof traps heat badly. Hang a wet cloth or mat over it if you can, and spend the hottest hours in the shade outside.
Stay indoors. Unplug appliances and avoid the phone on a wired line. Away from windows, balconies and open terraces until it passes.
Stay off the balcony and terrace, they carry the highest lightning risk in your building. Move to an inner room.
Drop, cover under something sturdy, and hold on until shaking stops. Stay away from windows and anything that can fall.
Do not run for stairs or lifts during shaking. Drop and cover where you are; leave the building calmly only after it stops.
Get away from the walls immediately if the structure is weak, an open space outside is safer than staying under a fragile roof.

occupation_tips.tip_text: Move livestock and stored grain to higher ground today. Shift pumps and fertiliser bags above the flood line.
Harvest what is ready and cover stored produce. Do not go to the fields during the storm.
Clear field drainage channels and postpone spraying or fertiliser for 48 hours.
Work the field only before 11am and after 4pm. Water livestock three times a day and keep them shaded.
Leave open fields immediately. Do not shelter under a lone tree or near metal fencing or farm equipment.
Do not go out to sea. Pull boats well above the high-tide line and secure fishing gear.
Check the latest sea-condition advisory before heading out, seas can turn rough with little warning in this weather.
Head to shore now if you're out. Lightning over open water is especially dangerous.
Ask for water breaks and shade every hour if working outdoors. Heat stroke can set in fast with no warning.
Outdoor and construction sites get dangerous in heavy rain, loose scaffolding and slippery surfaces especially. Ask about a delay if conditions look unsafe.
Come down from any height or scaffolding and move away from metal structures until it passes.
If you're on duty, expect higher patient load during and after this event, keep your own supplies and transport plan ready so you can stay.
Check the school's closure notice before sending children. If they're already there, collect them early, routes may close by evening.
Schools will likely close. Keep children indoors and away from windows.
Check for a closure notice and plan pickup before peak rain, avoid routes through underpasses.
Send children with a full water bottle and a cap, and check for revised school timings.
Keep children indoors and away from windows until it passes, and don't let them go back out for the school run yet.

elderly.*: Check on elderly family members every few hours and keep their regular medicines within reach.
elderly.heatwave: Elderly people overheat quickly. Keep them in the coolest room and give water, ORS or buttermilk regularly.

infant_or_pregnant.*: Keep a hospital bag, ID and any medical records ready in case you need to move quickly.
infant_or_pregnant.heatwave: Infants and pregnant women dehydrate faster. Keep them cool, hydrated, and watch for unusual drowsiness or reduced urination.

disability.*: Tell a neighbour or the helpline now if you need help to move. Keep mobility aids and medicines packed by the door.

chronic_illness.*: Keep at least a week's supply of your regular medicines and your prescription with you in case pharmacies are closed.

livestock.*: Move animals to a safe, sheltered spot and keep two days of fodder and water ready.
livestock.flood: Untie animals if you cannot move them. Tied animals drown; untied animals can swim to safety.
